title: External sources report
description: One run of the external sources view, as `wipctl sources --json` emits it: every declared source, the open items each one listed, which artifacts reference them, and how reference-form watches compare with the open list. A source whose command did not answer appears with its degradation named rather than omitted, so a consumer can tell an empty source from an unread one.

sources.description: One object per alias declared in the sources section of .wipctl/plan.toml, in the section's own order.

alias.description: The local name this plan gave the source. It is meaningful in this record alone.

answered.description: Whether the declared list command ran and produced readable output. False is a degradation and never a failure, so the report still exits zero.

degradation.description: Present exactly when answered is false: the same sentence the error stream carried, naming what did not answer and the reader's next step.

items.description: The open items the command listed, empty when the source answered with none and when it did not answer at all.

key.description: The item's own name in its system. It is opaque here, and no consumer parses its interior.

url.description: The address the alias's url template renders for this key. It is a substitution and never a guess.

referenced_by.description: The ids of this record's artifacts whose sources section names this item. Empty means no artifact claims it, which is the reason to read several lists at once.

watches.description: The reference-form watches using this alias. An empty array from an answered source means no watch of this alias is missing. A source that did not answer marks every watch unjudged.

id.description: The watch id from its section heading.

key.description: The opaque item key from the watch's source reference.

url.description: The address the alias's url template renders for this key.

mark.description: The comparison with the open list. No longer listed claims no remote state or satisfied exit condition.

skipped_watches.description: The phrase-form watches that have no alias or key to compare and must remain visible as skipped.

id.description: The watch id from its section heading.

mark.description: The view skipped comparison because the watch names an actor rather than a source reference.
